questions.scenario: VAT charged on Masco's local sales (Output) and paid on local purchases (Input) are best described as:
options: Company income and company expense
The state's money passing through — Output is a liability, Input is a recoverable asset; VAT never touches profit
Both permanent costs of production
Optional contributions
questions.explanation: Masco acts as collection agent: net Output-minus-Input goes to NBR monthly. Misclassifying VAT as income/expense inflates revenue/costs — a classic error this module kills.
wrongExplanations: It's never ours — custody, not ownership (the tax calendar's first commandment).
They wash against each other at settlement; neither reaches the P&L.
Registration and filing are mandatory even for zero-rated exporters.

questions.scenario: Exports to H&M are zero-rated for VAT. Practical meaning:
options: Masco charges H&M VAT in dollars
No output VAT on export invoices, with input VAT related to exports recoverable/offset — but registration, records, and RETURNS continue
VAT law doesn't apply to exporters at all
Input VAT becomes company profit
questions.explanation: Zero-rating changes the NET position, not the discipline: books, registers, and filings run exactly the same — a fact many new exporters learn late.
wrongExplanations: Export invoices carry no VAT line — that's the point of zero-rating.
Registered status with full documentation duties remains.
Recoverable input VAT offsets obligations; it isn't earnings.

questions.scenario: TDS vs AIT — which statement is correct?
options: Both are expenses of the company
TDS = WE withhold FROM payments we make (salaries, vendors); AIT = others withhold FROM our receipts (LC settlements, imports) as prepaid credits
AIT is optional if profit is low
TDS applies only to foreign suppliers
questions.explanation: Direction decides everything: withheld-by-us creates liabilities until challaned; withheld-from-us creates credit assets tracked certificate-wise against year-end liability.
wrongExplanations: Neither is an expense: one is pass-through custody, the other prepayment.
Statutory withholding regimes don't negotiate with profit levels.
Salary TDS on our own workers is the most familiar TDS of all.

questions.scenario: Late deposit of salary TDS already deducted from workers means:
options: No issue — it stays our money longer
Penalty/interest AND worker credit disputes — potentially paying twice for one obligation
Workers lose their tax credits forever
NBR deducts it from next year's refund automatically with no consequence
questions.explanation: Deducted TDS was NEVER Masco's money — holding it past due dates draws penalties while employees still demand their credit certificates, creating double pain.
wrongExplanations: It was state money from the moment of deduction.
Credits survive but the dispute cost lands on us.
Interest and penalties are separate cash events.

questions.scenario: The bond license allows duty-free yarn import BECAUSE:
options: Suppliers give discounts to loyal buyers
Inputs are promised to become EXPORTS — proven kg-by-kg via UD declarations backed by GRN/issue/export data
VAT zero-rating covers customs too
Banks guarantee the duty personally
questions.explanation: Bond is custody of a PROMISE: bonded inputs must trace into exported garments within permitted wastage norms. The evidence chain is warehouse data — Jamal's GRNs and issues.
wrongExplanations: Commercial discounts are unrelated to statutory duty exemption.
Customs duty and VAT are different instruments with different rules.
No personal guarantees — documentary accountability instead.

questions.scenario: Book profit is ৳12 crore, yet taxable income differs. Why?
options: Accounting profit is always wrong
Tax computation adjusts: disallowed items, different depreciation schedules, concessionary export rates, minimum-tax floors — a book-to-tax reconciliation
NBR uses random assessments
Profit should be recorded after tax only
questions.explanation: Two rulebooks measure one business: IFRS-shaped books vs tax statutes. The bridge schedule (CA-owned) documents every adjustment — which is why clean ERP categories matter so much.
wrongExplanations: Books follow accounting standards faithfully — they just answer a different question.
Assessments follow published law and documented positions.
Pre-tax profit is the standard presentation everywhere.

options: Voluntary donations when profits are good
A statutory share of profit provisioned annually, held in a fund with its own compliance rules — accrued as expense/liability during the year
Paying workers' personal income tax
Converting salaries into dividends
questions.explanation: Module 8's accrual meets Module 11's statements: WPPF provisions reduce distributable profit monthly-in-spirit, settle annually, and carry trustee-level obligations.
wrongExplanations: It's statutory — generosity has no role in its existence.
Workers' taxes are their own affair (though OUR TDS remits what we withheld).
WPPF is earned BY workers, not owned by them as shareholders.

questions.scenario: June budget changes TDS rates mid-year. A professional ERP responds by:
options: Developers editing hardcoded constants overnight
INSERTING dated rows into rate config tables (with source references + approvals); historical transactions keep the rates THAT WERE LAW when they occurred
Retrospectively recalculating all year's transactions
Asking suppliers which rate they prefer
questions.explanation: This is the module's design centerpiece: effective-dated config makes budget cycles routine inserts with full audit lineage — future-proof and backward-truthful simultaneously.
wrongExplanations: Hardcoded rates break silently and fail every audit question about 'which rate applied'.
Law generally applies prospectively; rewriting history falsifies records.
Rates come from statute, not negotiation.

questions.scenario: UD declaration needs: 48,000 kg bonded yarn consumed → 19,900 pcs exported. Which systems' data feeds this proof?
options: Only commercial team spreadsheets
GRN receipts + material issues + production output + export shipments — the integrated chain from Modules 0-6, aggregated item-wise
Buyer's own portal reports
Year-end physical count alone
questions.explanation: UD is the bond promise's receipt: consumption-to-export traceability assembled from operational documents. Fragmented data here = duty recovery exposure — integration IS compliance.
wrongExplanations: Spreadsheets lack document lineage and cross-verification.
Buyer portals know THEIR orders, not our bonded consumption.
Counts show stock, not the journey from import to export.

questions.scenario: Shirin's #1 standing instruction for the whole tax domain:
options: Memorize every current rate forever
Own the statutory calendar visibly, keep registers reconciled monthly, review dated rate tables within 30 days of each budget, verify specifics at nbr.gov.bd before acting
Delegate everything to software
Pay early on everything regardless of rules
questions.explanation: Structure endures, numbers expire: calendar + reconciled registers + dated config + source verification is the complete professional posture this site has built toward since Module 0.
wrongExplanations: Memorization decays every June — systems beat memory.
Software executes; humans own deadlines and judgment.
Early payment without correct computation creates its own messes.
